title: How Sweden's Social Democrats survived in the capital of capital
gist: Sweden's September 2026 election was far closer than polls suggested; the Social Democrats scored 28.1%, their worst since 1921, yet remain the largest party and face a hard coalition negotiation spanning the market-liberal Centre Party and the ex-communist Left. Rikard Westerberg argues the party survived through union ties, new migrant-community voters and pro-market pragmatism, so centrist pragmatists will keep governing Sweden whichever bloc wins.

insights.claim: Sweden's 2026 election was too close to call until all votes were counted, despite polls showing a substantial lead for the opposition of Social Democrats, Greens, Left and Centre Party.
insights.speaker: Rikard Westerberg
